correctness.rationale: For n even and m=m_n→∞ with n/2 types needing m coupons and n/2 needing m+1, Poisson thinning turns the two rescaled group completion times into independent Gamma(m,1) and Gamma(m+1,1) maxima. Their exact CDFs are (1−Q_m(u))^(n/2),(1−Q_(m+1)(u))^(n/2); center u_n uniquely solves (n/2)(Q_m+Q_(m+1))=1, scale b_n=u_n/(u_n−m). The density Mills bounds with error m/(u_n−m)^2→0 (Gamma CLT implies u_n−m≫√m) give Q_j(u_n+xb_n)/Q_j(u_n)→exp(−x) for both j. Thus Gumbel limit without restriction on growth of m. The Poisson-clock de-Poissonization is valid uniformly because u_n/b_n² <= 2 log n+O(1), bounding count fluctuations versus n b_n. Tail ratio Q_(m+1)/Q_m ~u_n/m and Gamma rate function I(r)=r−1−log r prove the three last-class competition regimes: r∞=1, r0=∞, finite alpha: I(r)=1/alpha, winner probability r/(1+r). Checked independent finite numerical gamma tails/center, ratio and group maximum CDF in four regimes, including m≫n; these illustrate, not prove, asymptotic conclusions. The alpha=0 joint CDF has an escaping coordinate, correctly not claimed as R² weak convergence.
residual_risks: Even n, equally sized disjoint groups, uniformly sampled types, adjacent quotas m and m+1 with m→∞; no rates, unequal groups, or arbitrary quota sequences.
